name: Smart TV for Browser
summary: A smart-TV home screen in the browser, with a phone as the remote.
what: A smart-TV home screen that runs in the browser. It boots with an animated power-on, opens on a 10-foot grid of app tiles that glow and scale on focus, and is driven like a TV: arrow keys or an on-screen D-pad, with OK, Back and Menu. Opening an app plays a launch splash and hands over to the channel's own website; after about 45 seconds idle, an ambient clock fades in.

facts.label: Runs in
facts.value: Any browser, installable as a PWA, full-screen

facts.label: Controls
facts.value: Arrow keys, Enter and Esc, or the on-screen remote; no mouse needed

facts.label: Settings
facts.value: Show or hide each app, change the tile size; kept in localStorage

facts.label: Getting back
facts.value: A companion extension adds a Home button and Alt+Shift+H to every channel site

flow.label: The apps
flow.note: one entry each in services.json: name, logo, link and background colour

flow.label: Spatial navigation
flow.note: norigin-spatial-navigation moves focus by geometry, mirrored onto real DOM focus

flow.label: The channel's own website
flow.note: opened directly after the launch splash; the companion extension brings you home

flowNote: Offline without build-tool coupling: a native manifest and a hand-written service worker cache the app shell.
decisions: Geometry-based spatial navigation: focus moves the way a remote expects, not in DOM order.
Motion drives the boot animation, the focus springs and the screensaver.
The only backend is a Cloudflare Durable Object per pairing code: phone and screen open a WebSocket to the same room, so pairing works on any network with no NAT negotiation.
